title: Multi-tenant SaaS — cloud-hosted B2B product
description: A multi-tenant B2B SaaS product running on a public cloud provider: managed Kubernetes hosting the application tiers, a managed relational database shared across tenants via row-level isolation, object storage for tenant file uploads and backups, IAM roles granting workload and human access, and a CI/CD pipeline that deploys straight to production. Seeded as a starting-point template for teams assessing this class of system.

risks.title: Cross-tenant data leak
risks.description: A flaw in access control, storage configuration or query scoping allows one tenant's data — records, files or backups — to become visible to another tenant or to the public internet.

risks.title: Compromise of the production cloud account
risks.description: An attacker obtains credentials or a foothold with administrative reach over the cloud account itself, gaining the ability to read, modify or destroy any resource in the production environment.

risks.title: Service disruption through runaway cloud cost
risks.description: An attacker drives up managed-service usage — compute autoscaling, egress, API calls — to the point where the monthly bill becomes unsustainable, forcing an emergency capacity cut that degrades service for every tenant.

attacks.title: Leaked cloud API key in the CI/CD pipeline
attacks.description: A long-lived cloud credential committed to a repository, logged in build output, or left in a pipeline configuration is discovered and reused by an attacker to call the cloud provider's API directly.

attacks.title: Exploitation of an over-privileged service account
attacks.description: A workload's IAM role was granted broader read or write access than the workload actually needs; an attacker who compromises that workload inherits the excess privilege and reaches resources belonging to other tenants.

attacks.title: Publicly exposed object-storage bucket
attacks.description: A storage bucket holding tenant file uploads or database backups is misconfigured with public or overly broad read access, allowing anyone with the bucket name or a guessed object path to retrieve its contents.

attacks.title: Supply-chain compromise of the CI/CD pipeline
attacks.description: A malicious or compromised third-party dependency, base container image, or pipeline plugin executes attacker-controlled code during the build, with the same deployment privileges as the legitimate pipeline.

attacks.title: Cost-based denial of wallet
attacks.description: An attacker deliberately triggers expensive, auto-scaling operations — large file processing jobs, expensive API endpoints, or egress-heavy requests — repeatedly enough to inflate the cloud bill far beyond its normal range.

references.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

defences.title: Least-privilege IAM roles for workloads and pipelines
defences.description: Every workload and pipeline identity is scoped to a role granting only the specific resources and actions it needs, reviewed on a fixed schedule rather than left as originally provisioned.

attack-leaked-cicd-key.rationale: A leaked key tied to a narrowly-scoped role limits what an attacker can reach even after the credential itself is compromised.

attack-overprivileged-iam.rationale: Directly removes the excess grants this attack depends on; residual risk comes from roles awaiting their next scheduled review.

defences.title: Centralised secrets manager with short-lived credentials
defences.description: Cloud API credentials used by the pipeline and workloads are issued as short-lived tokens from a secrets manager at run time, rather than stored as static keys in configuration or source control.

attack-leaked-cicd-key.rationale: Short-lived tokens sharply shrink the window in which a leaked credential is still valid, and static long-lived keys are removed from most of the pipeline entirely.

attack-supply-chain-cicd.rationale: Malicious code running mid-build still inherits the token's scope for that run, but no longer gains a durable, reusable credential to carry forward afterward.

defences.title: Automated public-access scanning for storage buckets
defences.description: A scheduled scan checks every storage bucket's access policy against an allow-list of expected configurations and alerts on any bucket found to be publicly readable or writable.

attack-exposed-bucket.rationale: Catches a misconfiguration within one scan cycle rather than leaving it exposed indefinitely; does not prevent the misconfiguration from happening in the first place.

defences.title: Software bill of materials and dependency scanning
defences.description: Every build produces a software bill of materials, and dependencies and base images are checked against known-vulnerability and known-malicious-package feeds before a build is allowed to deploy.

attack-supply-chain-cicd.rationale: Blocks dependencies already known to be malicious or vulnerable, but offers no protection against a novel, not-yet-flagged compromise.

defences.title: Automated tenant-isolation test suite
defences.description: A dedicated test suite runs against every deployment, attempting cross-tenant reads and writes using each tenant's own credentials, and blocks the release if any cross-tenant access succeeds.

attack-overprivileged-iam.rationale: Catches isolation failures that stem from an over-broad role being exercised through the application layer; does not catch direct, out-of-band API access with the same role.

attack-exposed-bucket.rationale: Exercises the application's own access paths to storage, but a bucket made public at the infrastructure layer is reachable outside any path the test suite drives.

defences.title: Legacy shared-schema isolation approach (superseded)
defences.description: An earlier isolation model that relied on application-level filtering of a single shared database schema and bucket prefix, rather than provider-enforced access boundaries. Superseded by per-tenant scoping but referenced here for historical context.

attack-exposed-bucket.rationale: Prefix-based filtering offered only superficial separation and did nothing to prevent the underlying bucket itself from being made public.

defences.title: Cyber insurance with cloud-incident coverage
defences.description: An annual policy covering breach-response costs, forensic investigation, business-interruption loss and a portion of unexpected cloud usage charges arising from a confirmed security incident.

attack-leaked-cicd-key.rationale: Policy deductible and sub-limits mean roughly a third of the loss on an incident reached through this path is reimbursed on average.

attack-denial-of-wallet.rationale: The policy's cloud-usage-spike rider covers only charges above a high threshold, so it offsets a modest share of a typical incident's cost.

defences.title: Budget alerts and per-tenant rate limiting
defences.description: Hard rate limits on expensive API endpoints per tenant, combined with budget alerts that page the on-call engineer when spend accelerates beyond the normal range for the time of day.

attack-denial-of-wallet.rationale: Per-tenant limits cap how much cost a single abusive actor can generate before being throttled, though a slow, low-and-steady abuse pattern can still stay under the alert threshold.
